pairing_basis: same repeat index; acquisition order alternates FFT->hybrid on repeats 0,2,4 and hybrid->FFT on repeats 1,3

same_grid_repeat_index_control_contrast.description: 32^3 random32 paired delta minus 32^3 random256 all-fallback paired delta at the same repeat index. Descriptive only: the initial-condition cases are distinct and were not randomized counterfactuals.

findings: median(FFT)-median(hybrid) is not the median of paired differences. For 16^3 random32 the summary sign flips: arm-median delta -0.202604 ms versus paired median +0.105317 ms.

32^3 random32's paired median total margin (+0.328142 ms) is smaller than the all-fallback random256 paired median (+1.475251 ms). Its aggregate +0.910103 ms arm-median margin therefore cannot be attributed to sparse arithmetic from these frozen data.

The all-fallback control spans -11.547093 to +14.940788 ms with zero sparse calls, directly demonstrating timing/control-path variation on the same 32^3 harness at a scale larger than the small random32 margin.

32^3 Taylor-Green has all five repeat-paired total deltas positive and paired median +24.782943 ms; its margin is materially larger than the all-fallback control median, so it remains a stronger candidate for provisioned-host revalidation, but this is not a causal or independent speedup certificate.
16^3 Taylor-Green also has five of five positive paired deltas and paired median +5.055615 ms, but the frozen matrix contains no same-grid zero-sparse 16^3 control.

Hybrid setup is generally slower in the small-margin cases; the apparent benefit, when present, is concentrated in the RK4 interval. However the all-fallback control also exhibits a positive paired RK4 median, so RK4 aggregate deltas alone do not isolate sparse-compute causality.
